Notes: No state individual income tax - AS 43.20 individual income tax repealed for tax years after 1978 (AS 43.20.015). No SS taxation possible.
Official AL DOR page lists federal Social Security benefits as exempt from Alabama income tax.
Ark. Code Ann. 26-51-404(b)(6) excludes Social Security benefits from gross income. DFA FAQ 209 PDF would not render for direct verification; statute cited as the primary source instead.
A.R.S. 43-1022(10) allows subtraction of Social Security/Tier 1 Railroad Retirement from AZ gross income; consistent with AZ DOR Form 140 instructions.

FTB Schedule CA (540) instructions subtract taxable federal Social Security from CA taxable income. Direct fetch of ftb.ca.gov returned 403; confirmed via search-indexed snippet of the same page plus secondary corroboration.

65+ subtracts all federally taxable Social Security with no AGI limit (tax.colorado.gov, TY2022+). Ages 55-64 get that full SS subtraction only at/below $75k single / $95k joint AGI; above that a $20,000 combined pension/SS cap remains and is not modeled. Under-55 is not a full SS subtraction; the 65+ flag maps under-65 onto the 55-64 threshold path. SB25-136 did not become law. Re-verified 2026-08-18 against the DOR page.

CT DRS Informational Publication 2025(7). Single/MFS threshold $75,000; MFJ/HOH/QSS $100,000. Below threshold, 100% exempt. Above threshold, a worksheet caps CT-taxable SS at no more than 25% of the federally taxable benefit - a smooth reduction, not a hard cliff.
Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits are not taxable in Delaware.
No state individual income tax (state constitution prohibits one).
Taxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement on the Federal return are exempt from Georgia Income Tax.
HI DOTAX 2025 Booklet A: SS and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement exempt (statutory basis HRS 235-7). PDF text would not extract cleanly; confirmed via search-indexed quote of the same booklet.
Full exclusion since Iowa Code 422.7 as amended by 2022 HF 2317, effective TY2023+, regardless of age or income.
ID Form 39R (2025, rev. 2026-03-02) has a subtraction line for Social Security/railroad benefits included in federal income.
IL DOR FAQ: the federally taxed portion of SS is subtracted back out; Illinois taxes none of it.
Indiana does not tax Social Security and railroad retirement benefits.
Effective for all taxable years commencing after December 31, 2023, social security benefits are not subject to Kansas income tax. Repealed the prior $75,000 AGI threshold.
SS subtracted on KY Schedule M line 10; full exemption, no threshold. (A separate $31,110/person exclusion applies to other retirement income, not SS.)
Social Security benefits that are taxed on your federal return may be excluded from Louisiana taxable income. No threshold.

Massachusetts gross income excludes Social Security benefits. mass.gov blocked direct fetch (403) on every URL tried; confirmed via search-indexed snippet plus AARP/SmartAsset/LegalClarity corroboration.
MD Technical Bulletin No. 51: SS/Railroad Retirement benefits fully subtractable on Form 502 line 12, no threshold.
Full SS subtraction on Schedule 1S, no income/age limit on the SS subtraction itself. (SS received does reduce the separate pension-income deduction cap - a different line item.)

SS excluded from the taxable retirement/pension calculation and is separately non-taxable (MI RAB 2026-1). michigan.gov blocked direct fetch (403); confirmed via search-indexed snippet plus secondary sources.

MN DOR TY2026 inflation-adjusted table, simplified-method threshold: Single/HOH $86,410; MFJ/QSS $110,780 (MFS $55,390 not stored). Below threshold, 100% subtracted; above, subtraction phases out 10% per $4,000 of AGI over the threshold until it disappears. MN also offers an alternate subtraction method with a different, lower threshold that filers may use if it produces a larger benefit - not modeled here.
100% exemption for SS retirement (age 62+) and SS disability (any age), effective TY2024 after the prior AGI-based limitation was repealed by 2023 legislation.
Mississippi does not tax Social Security, Railroad Retirement, public welfare, VA, or workers' comp benefits.

Flag for review. Since TY2024, Montana starts from federal taxable income, so Social Security is taxed exactly as the IRS taxes it - there is no MT-specific SS income threshold. The only related break is a general age-65+ subtraction ($5,660 in 2025, inflation-adjusted; $11,320 if both spouses 65+) that applies to any income, not SS specifically - hence both thresholds are blank. Classified partial only because that age-based break exists; functionally this is close to taxed, the weakest fit of any state with a nonzero exemption. A 2025 repeal bill (HB148) failed.
Full deduction of any SS included in federal AGI (Form D-400 Schedule S, Part B); no income limit.
AGI-based phase-out removed effective TY2021; deduction now available regardless of AGI (pre-2021 cap was $50k single/$100k MFJ, no longer applicable).
LB754 (2023) accelerated full exemption to TY2024+, one year earlier than the original LB873 phase-out schedule.
NH never taxed wages or retirement income. Its Interest & Dividends Tax (which never covered SS) was fully repealed effective TY2025. No individual income tax of any kind as of 2026.
Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits are not taxable under the New Jersey Income Tax. No threshold on SS itself.

NM Taxation & Revenue Dept, in effect since TY2022. Hard cliff: full exemption at/below threshold; fully taxed at ordinary NM rates (1.7%-5.9%) above it. MFS threshold is $75,000 (not stored); HOH uses the $150,000 figure (stored).
No state individual income tax - Nevada Constitution Art. 10 Section 1(9); corroborated by NV Dept. of Taxation FAQ.
NY subtracts 100% of federally taxable Social Security from state AGI; no income limit.
OH IT 1040/Schedule A deducts federally taxable Social Security in full; no income cap. (Ohio still taxes most other non-military retirement income.)
Full subtraction of federally taxable Social Security via Schedule 511-A; no income threshold.

ORS 316.054 provides full subtraction of SS/Tier 1 Railroad Retirement income; no income test. PDF body text would not render directly; relying on the statute citation plus consistent secondary sourcing.
PA's class-of-income PIT excludes Social Security outright - it is not one of PA's eight taxable income classes.

Must reach SSA full retirement age AND federal AGI below the cliff. TY2025 worksheet (born on or before 03/01/1959): single/HOH/MFS $107,000; MFJ/QSS $133,750. TY2026 figures not published as of 2026-08-18. The 65+ flag approximates FRA (~67); filers under 65 are taxed. Sources: RI Division of Taxation Advisory 2025-22 and 2025 Social Security worksheet.
SC Code 12-6-1120: federally taxed SS/Railroad Retirement benefits exempt from SC individual income tax; no threshold.
No state individual income tax.

No general individual income tax on wages/retirement income. TN's only personal income tax, the Hall Income Tax (interest & dividends only, never covered wages/SS), was fully repealed effective TY2021.
No state individual income tax; constitutional ban (Art. 8 Section 24-a, adopted Nov 2019).

UT TC-40 Social Security Benefits Credit (code AH): a nonrefundable credit of 4.5% of federally taxable SS that fully offsets UT tax on that income at/below threshold. Single $54,000; MFJ/HOH/QSS $90,000 (MFS $45,000 not stored). Phases out $0.025 per $1 of excess modified AGI above threshold. Cannot combine with UT's separate age-based Retirement Credit.
Any SS/Tier 1 Railroad Retirement included in federal AGI is subtracted in full; no income limit.

Act/S.51 (signed June 2025, retroactive to all of 2025) raised the full-exemption threshold to $55,000 single / $70,000 MFJ; the exemption phases out over roughly the next $10,000 of AGI above threshold. Moderate confidence: tax.vermont.gov blocked direct fetch (403) and a legislative fiscal-office PDF hit a TLS error; figures are corroborated via a bill-citing VTDigger report rather than a directly fetched official page.

No individual income tax today. Flag: WA enacted a new 9.9% individual income tax on income above a $1M standard deduction (SB 6346 / Ch. 238, Laws 2026, the Millionaires' Tax), effective Jan 1, 2028 (first payments 2029). The $1M threshold means this does not affect Social Security for any realistic retiree, so not_taxed stands, but WA is no longer an unconditional no-income-tax state starting 2028 - worth a revisit before then.

WI DOR: Social Security is not taxable, subtracted in full on Schedule SB; no age or income limit. Direct WebFetch failed repeatedly (network error); based on search-surfaced content from the same official domain (FAQ + Publication 126).

Phase-out schedule: filers at/below $50k single / $100k MFJ federal AGI have been 100% exempt since TY2022; above those thresholds the modification was 35% (TY2024), 65% (TY2025), reaching 100% for TY2026 and beyond. As of TY2026 the exemption is 100% for every filer regardless of income, so no residual threshold applies going forward.

No state individual income tax - WY Constitution Art. 15 Section 18 requires full credit for sales/ad valorem taxes already paid against any income tax, making one economically unworkable; the legislature has never enacted one. PDF text extraction was imperfect; corroborated by secondary legal sources quoting the same text.
